petition_no: APPEAL No. 237 OF 2019 & APPEAL No. 368 OF 2022
summary: Counsel on record for the Respondent(s) : Samir Malik Rimali Batra Nikita Choukse Divya Anand for Res. 1 Counsel on record for the Appellant(s) : Samir Malik Nikita Choukse Manuj Kaushik Iti Agarwal Divya Anand Paritosh Goel for App. 1 Counsel on record for the Respondent(s) : Ravi Parkash for Res. 1 1. Appeal No. 237 of 2019 has been filed by M/s DCM Textiles, a Unit of DCM Nouvelle Limited challenging the order dated 22.04.2019 in Case No. HERC/PRO-51 of 2017 passed by the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission. 2. Appeal No. 368 of 2022 has been filed by Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, challenging the order dated 22.04.2019 in Case No. HERC/PRO-51 of 2017 **(** hereinafter referred as **“Impugned Order”** ) passed by the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission. 3. Since these two appeals are cross appeals against the same order and are integrally connected, these are being disposed of by this Common Judgement. 4. For the sake of convenience, the description of the parties is given here under as per appeal No.237 of 2019. 8. The State Commission, passed the order on 22.04.2019, Impugned in the appeals and held that since application for enhancement of the contract demand 10. We have heard Mr. Fanish K. Jain, learned counsel on behalf of Appellant –DCM, Ms Nikita Choukse learned counsel on behalf of Appellant -HVPNL . We have also perused the impugned order, the documents placed on record, and the written submissions filed by the learned counsels on behalf of Appellant, and Respondent - HVPNL. _as per provision under Regulation 4.4.3 (2) (c) of the Electricity Supply Code notified by the Commission._ 19. The Appellant –DCM, vide its letter dated 02.02.2017 and 16.03.2017 addressed to HVPNL and DHBVN, requested for issuance of demand notice in line with “Supply Regulation, 2016” and appellant-DCM vide its letter dated 26.05.2017 to HVPNL, with a copy to DHBVN, referring to “Supply Regulation 2016”, requested for withdrawal of proportionate cost of augmentation of Transformer at 220 kV IA Hissar substation and proportionate cost of augmentation of conductor on 132 kV line from 220kV IA Hissar substation to 132 kV Beer substation and reduction in corresponding supervision charges. The Appellant – DCM in June 2017 then filed a petition (No 51 of 2017) before HERC seeking clarification and implementation of provision of 4.4 and 4.7 of “Supply Regulation, 2016”, which culminated in passing of the Impugned Order dated 22.04.2019. In the meantime, on 02.04.2018, the Appellant submitted an undertaking to deposit the required proportionate cost, in case petition is decided against them and requested for execution of work and it was only on 20.07.2018, demand for estimated cost (in line with their letter dated 04.05.2016) was communicated by HVPNL to Appellant – DCM. 26. Learned Counsel on behalf of HVPNL has disputed the reliance placed by the Appellant-DCM on the applicability “Supply Code 2014”, contending that as same was in force at all material times and the Appellant-DCM had never invoked, relied upon, or asserted the applicability of the “Supply Code, 2014”, same is not permissible to be relied upon for the first time before this Tribunal as it is a well-settled principle that the Court cannot create any new case at the appellate stage for either of the parties and reliance was placed in this regard on the judgment of the Supreme Court in “ _**Rama Kt. Barman v. Mohd. Mahim Ali**_ **2024 SCC OnLine SC 4083** as well as this Tribunal judgement dated 18.01.2019, **in “** _**ACB (India) Limited v. Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.”;**_ **, Appeal No. 279 of 2015 .** It is an established principle that new facts cannot usually be raised for the first time at the appellate stage, as appeals are not meant to introduce fresh factual disputes however new legal plea stand on a different footing. Statutory provisions, rules, and regulations have a binding effect even if they are pleaded for the first time at the appellate stage. It has been consistently held that pure questions of law, especially those involving statutory provisions or regulation can be raised at any stage even for the first time and must be applied by the court irrespective of whether they were pleaded earlier. The HERC (Electricity Supply Code) Regulations, 2014 ( “Supply Code 2014”), being statutory in nature, have binding effect and can be raised for the first time at the appellate stage. In fact the, DHBVNL application to State Commission for seeking approval of enhancement of Contract demand for the Appellate-DCM is also considering the provisions of “Supply Code, 2014” and therefore the Appellant referring to the applicability of “Supply Code, 2014” cannot held to be creating a new case at the Appellate stage or against the law. We find it unnecessary to delve any further on this contention of Respondent HVPNL, as our observations are not solely based on the provisions of “Supply Code, 2014” 31. Learned Counsel on behalf of Appellant – DCM has contended that since the State Commission Order dated 17.04.2015 mentions that Supply Regulations, 2005 and subsequent amendments thereof or its re-enactment shall be applicable so accordingly demand has to be raised in terms of “Supply Regulation, 2016”. In view of above deliberations, we do not find merit in these submission as enactment of “Supply Regulation, 2016” cannot take away vested substantive rights retroactively, unless the amendment is expressly retrospective or it extinguish those rights; whereas same is not discernible from the “Supply Regulation, 2016”. We are therefore of the considered view that there is no error in the Impugned Order with regard to applicability of “Supply Regulation, 2005” not of “Supply Regulation, 2016” for enhancement of contract demand of Appellant-DCM at 132 kV level. 36. The Captioned Appeals and pending IAs, if any, are disposed of in these terms.
title: DCM TEXTILES VERSUS DAKSHIN HARYANA BIJLI VITRAN NIGAM LIMITED & Ors
